failure_modes.drop: Object released unintentionally before reaching its target.
failure_modes.spill: Contents (liquid, granular) leave the container outside the target.
failure_modes.damage: Object or environment is damaged or left in an unsafe state.
failure_modes.collision: Unintended contact with furniture, objects or people.
failure_modes.wrong_target: Action completed on the wrong object, location or person.
failure_modes.wrong_info: Information stated or stored is incorrect.
failure_modes.quality: Action completed but below the stated quality criterion.
failure_modes.neglect: Required social behaviour omitted (not attending, no eye contact).
failure_modes.multiple_at_once: More than the specified quantity handled in one action.
failure_modes.assistance: A human performed or simplified part of the task (§3.7).
failure_modes.alternative_input: Natural interaction replaced by a less natural channel (§3.7.4).
failure_modes.unsafe_contact: Robot touches a person without the task asking for it.

MAN.Grasp.name: Grasp
MAN.Grasp.intent: Establish a stable hold on an object so it can be moved. The prerequisite of almost every manipulation task; rarely scored alone.
MAN.Grasp.success: Object is lifted clear of its support and held without slipping.
MAN.Grasp.not_judged: Grasp type, gripper, suction or any end-effector design. The sub-skills below classify the demand the OBJECT places on a grasp, not the technique the robot uses to meet it.

MAN.Grasp.Power.name: Power-demand grasp
MAN.Grasp.Power.intent: Hold objects whose weight or bulk needs the hand/gripper to enclose them and resist large loads (full milk carton, bag, pot).
MAN.Grasp.Power.success: As MAN.Grasp, with the object held stable through transport.
MAN.Grasp.Power.not_judged: Whether a palm, two arms, suction cups or a hook is used.

MAN.Grasp.Intermediate.name: Intermediate-demand grasp
MAN.Grasp.Intermediate.intent: Hold flat or thin-edged objects that must be pinched from the side — the Feix "lateral" family (plate rim, tray edge, card-like items).
MAN.Grasp.Intermediate.not_judged: Technique, including sliding the object to a table edge first.

MAN.Grasp.Precision.name: Precision-demand grasp
MAN.Grasp.Precision.intent: Hold small or thin objects that only fit between fingertips (cutlery, dishwasher tab, pen). Small contact area makes errors in pose costly.

MAN.Pick.name: Pick
MAN.Pick.intent: Take an object from where it is so it can be carried elsewhere. The single most common manipulation step in household tasks.
MAN.Pick.success: Object is removed from its support and held by the robot.
MAN.Pick.not_judged: Grasp technique, number of attempts within the time limit.

MAN.Place.name: Place
MAN.Place.intent: Put a held object down at a target so it stays there, usable and safe — as a person would set it down, not drop it.
MAN.Place.success: Object rests at the target location, stable, in a usable orientation, and was released (not thrown or dropped).
MAN.Place.not_judged: Trajectory, speed, whether the object was regrasped.

MAN.Insert.name: Insert
MAN.Insert.intent: Place an object into a receptacle that constrains its pose (slot, holder, socket). A Place with tight tolerance.
MAN.Insert.success: Object is fully seated in the receptacle.

MAN.Pour.name: Pour
MAN.Pour.intent: Transfer liquid or granular contents from one container into another — serving drinks, preparing food.
MAN.Pour.success: A meaningful amount (task-defined) of contents lands in the target container; spillage is scored separately as failure mode `spill`.

MAN.OperateArticulated.name: Operate articulated object
MAN.OperateArticulated.intent: Move the part of a fixture or container that is constrained to a hinge, slide or thread: doors, drawers, racks, lids, caps. Needed to reach what is inside or to leave the home in order.
MAN.OperateArticulated.success: The articulated part reaches the requested state (open enough to access / fully closed / cap removed).
MAN.OperateArticulated.not_judged: Whether the robot pushes, pulls, hooks or uses its base.

MAN.OperateControl.name: Operate control
MAN.OperateControl.intent: Actuate a button, switch, knob or lever to make a device do something (start a washing machine, switch a light, boil a kettle).
MAN.OperateControl.success: The device changes state as intended.

MAN.Transport.name: Transport
MAN.Transport.intent: Move one or more objects between places while keeping them secure, possibly using a carrier (tray, basket).
MAN.Transport.success: All transported items arrive at the destination without loss.

MAN.Fold.name: Fold
MAN.Fold.intent: Turn a loose piece of clothing into a compact, regular folded shape.
MAN.Fold.success: Garment meets the task's fold-quality criterion.
MAN.Fold.not_judged: Folding sequence, tools on the robot.

MAN.Stack.name: Stack
MAN.Stack.intent: Arrange items on top of each other in a neat, stable pile.
MAN.Stack.success: Stack is stable and items are aligned to the task criterion.

MAN.Wipe.name: Wipe surface
MAN.Wipe.intent: Clean a surface (table, counter) by moving a tool or cloth over it.
MAN.Wipe.success: Target area is visibly cleared of the defined dirt.

NAV.Navigate.name: Navigate
NAV.Navigate.intent: Move to a named or perceived place in the home safely; the glue of every multi-room task.
NAV.Navigate.success: Robot stops within the task's tolerance of the goal, without collision.
NAV.Navigate.not_judged: Planner, path shape, speed within safety limits.

NAV.Follow.name: Follow person
NAV.Follow.intent: Keep up with a walking person to a destination they choose.
NAV.Follow.success: Robot arrives with the person without losing or contacting them.

NAV.Guide.name: Guide person
NAV.Guide.intent: Lead a person to a destination, adapting to their pace.
NAV.Guide.success: Person arrives at the destination together with the robot.

NAV.AvoidObstacle.name: Avoid obstacle
NAV.AvoidObstacle.intent: Reach a goal despite unexpected objects, restricted zones or people in the way. Scored by outcome (no contact), not by detecting the obstacle.
NAV.AvoidObstacle.success: No contact with the obstacle and goal still reached.
NAV.AvoidObstacle.not_judged: Whether the obstacle was detected explicitly.

NAV.SignalIntent.name: Signal motion intent
NAV.SignalIntent.intent: Make the robot's movement legible to people around it, e.g. by looking where it is going.
NAV.SignalIntent.success: The intended direction is visibly indicated during motion.

OBJ.Recognize.name: Recognize object
OBJ.Recognize.intent: Tell which object (or class) is in front of the robot, so it acts on the right thing.
OBJ.Recognize.success: Robot communicates the correct identity/class to the referee.

OBJ.DetectPlacement.name: Determine placement
OBJ.DetectPlacement.intent: Decide where an object belongs — free space on a surface, or the shelf holding semantically similar items.
OBJ.DetectPlacement.success: Robot indicates a location that satisfies the task's rule.

OBJ.DetectEvent.name: Detect event
OBJ.DetectEvent.intent: Notice a non-speech signal from the home (doorbell, alarm, knock).
OBJ.DetectEvent.success: Robot reacts to the event within the task's time window.

OBJ.EstimatePose.name: Estimate object pose
OBJ.EstimatePose.intent: Find an object's 3D position and orientation to plan an action on it.
OBJ.EstimatePose.success: Downstream action succeeds; not scored on its own.

OBJ.DetectAbsence.name: Detect absence
OBJ.DetectAbsence.intent: Notice that something expected is missing (a guest without a drink).
OBJ.DetectAbsence.success: Robot correctly reports the missing item or class.

PPL.Detect.name: Detect person
PPL.Detect.intent: Know that a person is present and where.
PPL.Detect.success: Robot orients to / reports each person in scope.

PPL.DetectGesture.name: Detect gesture
PPL.DetectGesture.intent: Recognise a deliberate bodily signal (waving, calling, pointing).
PPL.DetectGesture.success: Robot reacts to the correct person's gesture.

PPL.DetectActivity.name: Detect activity
PPL.DetectActivity.intent: Recognise what people are doing when they are not signalling the robot — a conversation has ended, a guest is wearing shoes, someone entered — so the robot can choose when and whom to approach.
PPL.DetectActivity.success: Robot reacts to the correct person's state within the task's time window.

PPL.ResolvePointing.name: Resolve pointing
PPL.ResolvePointing.intent: Work out which object or place a person is pointing at.
PPL.ResolvePointing.success: Robot names or acts on the object/place the person meant.

PPL.DescribeAttribute.name: Describe person
PPL.DescribeAttribute.intent: Tell a visual attribute of a person (clothing, hair, height).

PPL.Reidentify.name: Re-identify person
PPL.Reidentify.intent: Recognise a person met earlier, by face, voice or appearance.

HRI.Attend.name: Attend to people
HRI.Attend.intent: Show awareness of the people the robot interacts with — acknowledge them, face them, do not ignore them.
HRI.Attend.success: Each person in the interaction is acknowledged.
HRI.Attend.not_judged: Exact behaviour used to acknowledge, and gaze quality — that is scored by HRI.Gaze lines. A neglect penalty here means the robot did not engage at all: it ignored, turned away from, or never responded to the person.

HRI.Gaze.name: Social gaze
HRI.Gaze.intent: Look at the person speaking or being spoken about.
HRI.Gaze.success: Head/gaze is visibly directed at the correct person.

HRI.Handover.name: Handover
HRI.Handover.intent: Pass an object to, or take it from, a person directly — without the person having to adapt to the robot's mechanics.
HRI.Handover.success: Object changes hands without being dropped or placed on the robot.

HRI.Indicate.name: Indicate
HRI.Indicate.intent: Direct a person's attention to a place or object (offer a free seat, show where something is).
HRI.Indicate.success: Person understands which place/object is meant.

HRI.ConveyInfo.name: Convey information
HRI.ConveyInfo.intent: Tell a person something the robot learned earlier — a guest's name, a customer's order, a summary of what happened — correctly and to the right person.
HRI.ConveyInfo.success: All required items are stated correctly to the intended person.

HRI.Explain.name: Make state visible
HRI.Explain.intent: Show people what the robot perceives, hears and intends — camera view, recognised objects, speech-to-text, current subtask, planned path — so referees and users can follow and trust it.
HRI.Explain.success: The required information is shown live and matches what the robot does.

HRI.Interrupt.name: Stop on request
HRI.Interrupt.intent: Stop the current action at once when a person says "stop" or touches the robot, and resume only when told to. The basic safety contract with untrained users.
HRI.Interrupt.success: Motion halts within the task's reaction time; resumes on the agreed trigger.

NLU.UnderstandCommand.name: Understand command
NLU.UnderstandCommand.intent: Turn a spoken request from a non-expert into an actionable goal, despite paraphrase and noise.
NLU.UnderstandCommand.success: Robot repeats or acts on a correct interpretation.

NLU.ExtractInfo.name: Extract information
NLU.ExtractInfo.intent: Pick out and store facts a person states (name, favourite drink, order, where something is).
NLU.ExtractInfo.success: Stored facts are later reproduced correctly.

NLU.Clarify.name: Clarify efficiently
NLU.Clarify.intent: Ask only the questions needed to remove ambiguity — not burden the user with confirmations.

PLN.Plan.name: Plan
PLN.Plan.intent: Decompose a goal into a sequence of executable skills.
PLN.Plan.success: Robot communicates a plan that would achieve the goal.

PLN.Execute.name: Execute task
PLN.Execute.intent: Carry a multi-step command through to its goal state.
PLN.Execute.success: Goal conditions of the command hold at the end. Partial completion is scored by goal predicates, not referee impression.
PLN.Execute.not_judged: Order of steps unless the command fixes it.

PLN.Interleave.name: Interleave tasks
PLN.Interleave.intent: Work on several commands at once when it saves time.
PLN.Interleave.success: Steps of different commands are interleaved and all goals hold.

GEN.HumanAssistance.name: Human assistance
GEN.HumanAssistance.intent: Not a robot capability. Records that a human did part of the task, so the score reflects only what the robot did itself (§3.7).

GEN.AlternativeInput.name: Alternative interaction channel
GEN.AlternativeInput.intent: Not a robot capability. Records that the robot used a less natural input channel than speech with the default operator (§3.7.4).

GEN.UnsafeConduct.name: Unsafe conduct
GEN.UnsafeConduct.intent: Not a skill. Records that the robot endangered a person, so safety has a price in the score and not only in the stop it causes (league draft #90).

GEN.TaskConstraint.name: Task-specific constraint
GEN.TaskConstraint.intent: Not a skill. A task-level rule whose violation is penalised (e.g. the breakfast must look like a typical meal setting).

SPECIAL.Administrative.name: Administrative
SPECIAL.Administrative.intent: Rulebook §3.8 lines that are not robot capabilities.

sources.Feix2016: T. Feix, J. Romero, H.-B. Schmiedmayer, A. M. Dollar, D. Kragic, "The GRASP Taxonomy of Human Grasp Types", IEEE Trans. Human-Machine Systems 46(1), 2016. Used for the power / intermediate / precision split only.

mass.question: How heavy is the object (with contents)?

medium.guide: 250–1000 g — cans, soju bottle, small milk carton

size.question: Across its narrowest graspable dimension, how big is the object?

thin.guide: < 15 mm — cutlery handle, plate rim, cloth

surface.question: How easily does the surface slip?

smooth.guide: glazed ceramic, glossy plastic, metal, glass

rigidity.question: Does the object keep its shape when held?

compliant.guide: bags, pouches, fragile items that must not be squeezed

deformable.guide: clothing, towels — shape changes with every grasp

shape.question: Is there an obvious place to hold it?

irregular.guide: concave or asymmetric — bowl, mug by the body

flat_lying.guide: lies flush on its support — plate, flat cloth

contents.question: Does the object contain something that constrains its motion?

upright.guide: open container with liquid/granular content, must stay level

mechanism.question: (articulated objects / controls) What kind of motion does it need?

guided.guide: hinge or slide — door, drawer, rack

latched.guide: needs a handle/latch/thread released first — handle door, screw cap

actuation_force.question: (articulated objects) How much force does it take?

reach.question: Where is the object or the target?

enclosed.guide: inside an appliance, drum, cabinet or rack

knowledge.question: Has the robot seen (or heard) this exact thing before — object, sound, person, word?

known_instance.guide: exact object/sound/person/phrase published before the test

known_class.guide: category known, instance not — 'any traditional doorbell', 'any popular English name'

unknown.guide: never seen, category not given — a drink not on the object list

placement_tolerance.question: How exact must the final pose be?

region.guide: anywhere in an area or on a surface

spot.guide: a specific spot or semantic group — next to the bowl, with similar items

constrained.guide: a slot, rack tines, aligned stack, cleanable orientation

carrier.question: Is a loose carrier used for transport?

none.guide: object held directly or in a fixed robot container

unattached.guide: loose tray or basket that must itself be balanced

map_knowledge.question: How well does the robot know the space?

moved.guide: furniture may have moved, location given at runtime

crowd.question: How many people move around the robot?

obstacle_visibility.question: How hard are obstacles to perceive?

hard_to_see.guide: transparent, thin, reflective, or a marked no-go area with no physical boundary

input_variability.question: How varied is the language the robot must understand?

route_extent.question: How far, topologically, does the robot travel?

room.guide: within one room or one open space (a restaurant floor)

building.guide: corridors, lifts, or out of the arena and back

perception_range.question: How far away is the person, object or signal to perceive?

near.guide: ≤ 1.5 m, in front of the robot

far.guide: across a large space or another room; must be searched for

target_motion.question: Does the person the skill is aimed at move?

shifting.guide: sways, paces, changes seat — 'guests move slightly'

walking.guide: walks freely while the skill runs

distractors.question: How many plausible wrong answers are present?

none.guide: only one candidate person, object, place or class

few.guide: a few candidates, easy to tell apart

similar.guide: several near-identical candidates — identical chairs, look-alike guests, neighbouring shelf categories

ambient_noise.question: How noisy is it where the robot listens?

background.guide: arena during a test — spectators, other people talking

loud.guide: public venue, music, several people speaking at once

info_load.question: How many separate items must be understood, stored or stated in this line?

single.guide: one item — a name, one attribute

few.guide: 2–3 items — name and drink, a two-object order

many.guide: 4 or more — a summary, several people's details

retention.question: How long must the robot keep the information before using it?

immediate.guide: used in the same exchange it was learned in

task.guide: used later in the task, after other activity

long.guide: used in another task, or after the person changed place or appearance

plan_length.question: How many skills must be chained to reach the goal?

long.guide: 5 or more, or a search with an unknown number of steps
